sections.h2: How is a Wyoming house sale organized?
sections.html:
Wyoming has 23 counties, and almost every step of a house sale runs through the one where the property sits. Laramie County is the largest by population at 102,938 people, and Niobrara County is the smallest at 2,341, according to the Wikipedia county list built on Census figures.

The county seat is not always the biggest town. Green River, not Rock Springs, is the seat of Sweetwater County. When you need a tax bill, a recorded deed or an assessment notice, you call the offices at the county seat. Our pages cover Cheyenne, Casper, Gillette and Laramie, and the county list further down shows where each one sits.

sections.h2: Who values, bills and collects property tax on a Wyoming house?
sections.html:
Three different offices touch your tax. The county assessor values the property, local districts set the mill levies, and the county treasurer sends the bill and takes the payment. If a number looks wrong, the office you call depends on which number it is.

Here is what the state sources we reviewed say:

  • Residential property is assessed at 9.5 percent of market value, and industrial property at 11.5 percent.
  • Value is set as of January 1 each year.
  • Tax is paid in two halves, payable by November 10 and May 10.
  • A late balance accrues interest at 18 percent a year.
  • Unpaid real property tax is a lien on the house, and the county can sell the lien at a tax sale.

The Department of Revenue says an appeal of an assessment has to argue market value, not the tax rate, and has to include evidence. Objections start with the county assessor and then go to the county board of equalization. Our Wyoming property tax guide walks through the deadlines.

When you sell, ask the treasurer for a payoff figure before closing. Because the lien stays with the house, back tax is normally paid out of the sale proceeds. We have written county guides for Campbell County and Sweetwater County. For any other county, call the treasurer at the courthouse and confirm the current due dates and interest, since local practice can differ.

sections.h2: Is foreclosure in Wyoming judicial or non-judicial?
sections.html:
Most Wyoming mortgages are foreclosed by advertisement and sale, which means the lender does not have to sue first. Chapter 4 of Title 34 of the Wyoming Statutes sets the steps, and a seller facing a sale date should read them with an attorney.

StepWhat the statute says
Before publicationWritten notice of intent to foreclose goes by certified mail to the record owner and anyone in possession at least 10 days before publication starts.
PublicationThe sale notice runs for four consecutive weeks, at least once a week, in a newspaper printed in the county.
Mailed copyA copy goes to the owner, any occupant and junior lienholders at least 25 days before the sale.
RedemptionThree months from the sale date, with interest at 10 percent a year.
Agricultural landTwelve months, for parcels over 80 acres outside a town or subdivision or used mainly for farming.

Two practical points follow. First, an owner can still sell the house on the open market or to a cash buyer before the sale date, and the payoff to the lender comes out of the proceeds at closing. Second, if a foreclosure sale produces more money than the lender is owed, the lender must send the sale results to the owner and junior lienholders within 10 business days.

These timelines can change, and notices have to match the statute exactly. Confirm the current text and your own dates with a Wyoming attorney or the lender before relying on them.

sections.h2: What does the homestead exemption do for a Wyoming seller?
sections.html:
Wyoming law protects up to $100,000 of a resident's homestead value from execution and attachment for most debts. That figure comes from W.S. 1-20-101 in the 2025 statutes published on Justia.

The exemption is a shield against creditors, not a rule about how a sale must happen. It does not erase a mortgage or a tax lien, and it does not tell you what a buyer will pay. If you owe other debts and plan to sell, ask an attorney how the exemption interacts with a judgment lien before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: Can you sell a Wyoming house that has tenants or an occupant who will not leave?
sections.html:
Yes, but the buyer takes the problem along unless you resolve it first. Wyoming has a fast court process for removing an occupant, and a few rules matter before you list.

  • A notice to quit must be served at least 3 days before a forcible entry and detainer action starts.
  • That action can reach an occupier of land who has no color of title and no right to possession.
  • An action to recover title or possession of land generally has to be filed within 10 years of when the claim accrued.
  • Criminal trespass is a misdemeanor, with up to 6 months in jail and a fine of up to $750.

Our Wyoming squatters rights and adverse possession guide explains these rules in more detail. Rental houses add lease terms, deposits and notice periods, so read the lease and ask the county or circuit court clerk about forms before you act.

sections.h2: What does selling as-is for cash mean in Wyoming?
sections.html:
It means the buyer takes the house in its current condition and you skip the repairs, showings and listing prep. In a state with long winters and dry, windy weather, that matters for houses that have gone a season without upkeep.

Inspectors and buyers in Wyoming tend to look first at:

  • Roofing and flashing, which take a beating from wind and freeze and thaw cycles.
  • Furnace age and insulation, because heating season is long.
  • Foundation cracks and drainage where snowmelt collects.
  • Well and septic systems on lots outside municipal service.

A cash buyer prices those items in rather than asking you to fix them. Cash Home Buyers works with owners in Cheyenne, Casper, Gillette, Laramie and across the rest of the state. Whatever route you pick, a title company or closing attorney will confirm who owns the property, clear liens and record the deed with the county clerk.

sections.h2: Who do you call about a Wyoming house sale?
sections.html:
Wyoming is a county based state, so a short call list saves time. The table below matches each question to the office that normally answers it.

QuestionOffice to call
What is my house valued at?County assessor
How much tax is due and is it paid?County treasurer
Where is the deed recorded?County clerk
Can I appeal my value?Assessor first, then the county board of equalization
Is the foreclosure notice valid?A Wyoming attorney

We could not confirm a state transfer tax figure or a probate timeline from an official page we opened, so ask the county clerk, the closing company or an attorney about those. If the house came to you through an estate, expect to need court paperwork that shows you have authority to sell.

When you are ready to compare options, a cash offer is one of them. Tell us the address and the situation, and a team member will walk through the next steps with you.

faqs.q: How many counties does Wyoming have?
faqs.a: Wyoming has 23 counties. Laramie County is the most populous at 102,938 people and Niobrara County is the smallest at 2,341.

Most Wyoming mortgages are foreclosed by advertisement and sale under Title 34, Chapter 4, so the lender does not have to file a lawsuit first. The sale notice runs for four consecutive weeks in a county newspaper.

faqs.q: Can I get my house back after a foreclosure sale in Wyoming?
faqs.a: Usually you have three months from the sale date to redeem, paying the bid plus 10 percent yearly interest. Qualifying agricultural land gets twelve months. Check the dates with an attorney.

faqs.q: When are Wyoming property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is payable by November 10 and the second half by May 10. A late balance accrues interest at 18 percent a year, so ask the county treasurer for current figures.

faqs.q: How much of my home is protected by the Wyoming homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The 2025 statute protects up to $100,000 of homestead value from execution and attachment for most debts. It does not remove a mortgage or tax lien.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Wyoming house with an occupant who will not leave?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer inherits the situation unless it is resolved first. A notice to quit must be served at least 3 days before a forcible entry and detainer action begins.
The buyer accepts the house in its current condition, so you do not make repairs before closing. Title and recording still go through the usual county process.
